clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old female presented with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain with a negative MRCP workup. Approximately one week after kidney biopsy, bilateral eye redness developed, consistent with anterior uveitis confirmed by ophthalmologic examination showing keratic precipitates and posterior synechiae. Laboratory findings revealed significant proteinuria (900 mg/dL) and elevated serum creatinine (2.5), indicating renal involvement. Kidney biopsy demonstrated marked interstitial infiltrate with tubulitis and focal tubular epithelial necrosis, consistent with acute interstitial nephritis. Treatment with systemic prednisone and topical prednisolone was initiated. Clinical improvement was documented three weeks later with reduced proteinuria (100 mg/dL) and improved creatinine (1.8). These findings confirm the diagnosis of TINU syndrome.
